title: Point the docs sys.path at src/, resolved from conf.py
body:
`docs/source/conf.py` put the **repository root** on `sys.path`, but the package lives in `src/`. So `import ivert` never resolved to the working tree — a local `sphinx-build` documented whatever copy happened to be installed in the environment, or failed with `ModuleNotFoundError` when nothing was.

Read the Docs was unaffected, because `uv sync --group docs` installs the checkout itself. The failure only shows up locally, which is exactly when someone is trying to verify a docs change before pushing.

The path is also now resolved from `__file__` rather than a relative `"../.."`, which depended on Sphinx's working directory at the time `conf.py` is executed.

```python
- sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("../..").resolve()))
+ sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "src"))
```

## Testing

Built with **no `ivert` installed anywhere** — not in the environment, not editable — so `conf.py` was the only route to the package:

- `python -c "import ivert"` → `ModuleNotFoundError`, confirming nothing was installed.
- `sphinx-build -E -b html docs/source/ …` → `build succeeded`, and the generated CLI page contains the real introspected options (`--classes`, `--min-photons`), proving `sphinx-click` imported the working tree.

The one remaining warning on this branch is the unescaped-asterisk issue in `cli_usage.md`, fixed separately in #86.

title: Add import netCDF4 to icesat2_database
body:
This PR adds `import netCDF4` to the very top of icesat2_database_v2.py

## Reasoning
In a clean venv environment when ivert is installed via pip; the netcdf5 and h5py libraries have conflicting libhdf5 binary wheels. Due to this, `ivert database download` would crash in a venv environment with an error such as:

```
  File "src/netCDF4/_netCDF4.pyx", line 2680, in netCDF4._netCDF4.Dataset.close
  File "src/netCDF4/_netCDF4.pyx", line 2647, in netCDF4._netCDF4.Dataset._close
  File "src/netCDF4/_netCDF4.pyx", line 2164, in netCDF4._netCDF4._ensure_nc_success
RuntimeError: NetCDF: HDF error
```

This would not happen in a conda environment because conda supplies a standard libhdf5 library for both xarray and h5py to use.

see:
https://github.com/pydata/xarray/issues/4277
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/63142417/python-xarray-and-h5py-incompatibility

Importing netCDF5 at the top of this file fixes this issue.

## Test
Install ivert in a venv with pip and `ivert database download` will complete successfully now.

title: Read "NaN" and "inf" config values as floats, not strings
body:
## The crash

Validating a DEM whose header declares no NoData value, without passing `--ndv`, died inside the validation child process:

```
File ".../validate_dem.py", line 1253, in _compute_photon_overlap
  if numpy.isnan(dem_ndv):
TypeError: ufunc 'isnan' not supported for the input types, and the inputs
could not be safely coerced to any supported types according to the casting rule ''safe''
```

The workaround was to pass `--ndv nan` explicitly.

## Root cause

`dem_ndv` falls back to the `dem_default_ndv` setting, which `ivert_defaults.ini` sets to `NaN` and documents as a float:

```ini
# "NaN" treats not-a-number cells as nodata; a numeric value (e.g. -9999)
# treats that value as nodata instead.
dem_default_ndv = NaN
```

`Config._read_option()` parses values with `ast.literal_eval()`, which covers every Python *literal* — but `NaN` and `inf` are **names**, not literals, so the parse raised `ValueError` and the value fell through to the closing "probably just a regular string" branch. The setting arrived as the string `'NaN'`, and no arithmetic on it could work.

So the fault was in the config parser, not in `validate_dem.py`: the `.ini` clearly intends a float and the parser silently produced a string.

## The fix

Convert non-finite floats after the `literal_eval` attempt:

```python
if isinstance(value, str):
    try:
        number = float(value)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        if not math.isfinite(number):
            setattr(self, key, number)
            return
```

The `isfinite` guard is the load-bearing part. A bare `float()` fallback would look simpler but is unsafe: `float("007")` is `7.0`, so an unquoted `nsidc_atl_version = 007` in a user config — which NSIDC requires as a zero-padded *string* — would silently become the number 7. Restricting the conversion to non-finite values covers exactly what `literal_eval` cannot express, and nothing else.

## Testing

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `dem_default_ndv` | now `nan` (float), was `'NaN'` (str) |
| `nsidc_atl_version`, `atl24_date_cutoff`, `verbosity`, `export_error_formats`, `icesat2_vertical_datum`, `ivert_results_subdir` | types unchanged |
| Unquoted `nsidc_atl_version = 007` in a user config | still `'007'` (str), not `7.0` |
| `dem_default_ndv = -9999` in a user config | still `-9999` (int), as the `.ini` comment documents |
| DEM with no NoData in its header, no `--ndv` | now runs, RMSE 18.538 m — identical to the earlier `--ndv nan` workaround run |
| DEM declaring `-9999` NoData | still runs, RMSE 18.538 m |
| `prek run --all-files` | passes |

The now-redundant `float(EMPTY_VAL)` at `validate_dem.py:2176` is left alone: it is a harmless no-op, and still does real work if someone sets an integer nodata.

Found while fixing #77; independent of #78, and touches no file that PR changes.

title: Catch a missing photon database in "ivert validate" instead of crashing
body:
Fixes #77.

## The crash

`ivert validate` against a missing database died with two stacked tracebacks ending in:

```
File ".../icesat2_database_v2.py", line 914, in query_photons
  logger.info("Reading %d granules overlapping %r.", len(gdf_subset), bbox)
TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()
```

`query_granules()` returns `None` when there is no index file, and `query_photons()` then calls `len()` on it — inside a validation child process, hence the doubled traceback.

## The fix

`_run_validate()` now calls the new `IS2Database.ensure_index_exists()` after argument validation and before any DEM is opened:

* index present → nothing to do.
* index missing, but granules on disk → warn and rebuild the index in place.
* neither one → a `click` error naming both configured paths.

The error message:

```
Error: No IVERT ICESat-2 photon database exists where IVERT is looking for it. Neither the index file nor any .nc granule files were found.
  index file:         /…/granules/_ivert_database_index.nc
  granules directory: /…/granules
Run 'ivert database download <bbox or DEM>' to begin creating an IVERT database, or point IVERT at an existing one with 'ivert options ivert_database_directory=<path>'.
```

The rebuild warning:

```
The database index '_ivert_database_index.nc' is missing, but 8 granule file(s) are present in /…/granules. Rebuilding the index in place; this may take a few moments.
```

Both paths are reported because `ivert_database_index` and `ivert_database_directory` are separate settings and need not point at the same place.

## Also

The index file lives in the granules directory and also ends in `.nc`, so the new `IS2Database.granule_files()` skips it by name. `create_new_database()` now shares that helper; it previously listed the directory itself, and only avoided counting the index as a granule because it deletes the index before listing.

## Testing

* Empty database directory, and a database directory that does not exist → the error above, exit 1.
* 8 granules with the index deleted → warning, index rebuilt with 8 records, and the validation ran through to completion (464 photons, RMSE 18.538 m, all outputs written). A second run is silent.
* `ivert database rebuild` and `ivert database list` still work after the `granule_files()` refactor.
* `prek run --all-files` passes.

title: Offer to save Earthdata credentials on download; quiet the "options --yes" warning
body:
Two small client-side fixes.

## Offer to save Earthdata credentials during `ivert database download`

A download that needs NASA Earthdata credentials prompted for them on every
run. The prompt comes from fetchez, which only *reads* `~/.netrc` and never
writes one, so there was no way to make the prompt stop from inside a
download — saving credentials was reachable only via `ivert setup`.

`database download` now offers to save them, and the helper that does it grew
two knobs so it can be reused from both call sites:

- `_stdin_is_interactive()` suppresses prompting when there is no tty.
- `_check_netrc_permissions()` warns and offers `chmod 600` when `.netrc` is
  group- or world-readable. This mattered more than it looks: stdlib `netrc`
  (what fetchez uses) refuses to parse such a file and reports *no*
  credentials, while IVERT's own `_has_earthdata_credentials()` parses tokens
  by hand and reports "all set" — so the user got reprompted forever with no
  explanation.
- `_setup_earthdata_credentials()` takes `announce_if_present` and
  `prompt_note`, and returns a bool. `ivert setup` calls it with the defaults
  and behaves exactly as before.

## Don't warn about dependent settings when `ivert options --yes` is used

`ivert options <key>=<value> --yes` printed the warning about settings that
inherit the changed value, and then updated them all anyway. That warning
exists to tell the user those settings would silently stay behind, which is
not what happens under `--yes`. The check now runs before the warning is
printed; the `Updated: ...` summary still reports what changed, and the
interactive and non-interactive paths are untouched.

## Testing

- `ivert options user_data_directory=... --yes` against a temp user config:
  no warning, five dependent settings updated and written.
- Same command without `--yes`: warning and prompt unchanged, dependents left
  at their defaults when declined.
- `prek run --files src/ivert/cli.py` passes.

title: Derive "ivert setup" directories from the config instead of hard-coding them
body:
Stacked on #71 — **base branch is `config-option-inheritance`**, so review that one first. The diff here is just the second commit.

## The problem

`ivert setup` carried two hand-maintained tuples:

```python
dir_attrs = ("user_data_directory", "cache_directory",
             "ivert_database_directory", "icesat2_download_directory")
file_attrs = ("ivert_database_index", "icesat2_requests_csv")
```

Any new path setting had to be added by hand, or it would silently never get created. This was flagged as a follow-up when `ivert setup` was added in #46.

## The change

`Config._read_option` already decides, per setting, whether a value is a local filesystem path — it's the same test that converts the value to an absolute path. It just wasn't recording the verdict. Now it does, exposed as `Config.path_options` (configfile order), and `setup` derives its work from it:

- a `*_directory` setting names a directory to create
- any other path setting names a file, so its parent directory is created

## Equivalence

Produces **exactly the same set of directories** as the tuples, verified against the default config, a relocated data tree, and an alternate `--config` file:

```
default:   IDENTICAL set
relocated: IDENTICAL set
altconfig: IDENTICAL set
```

The only behavioral change is the order they're reported in — configfile order rather than tuple order (`~/.ivert` now prints alongside the other `~/.ivert` entries instead of last).

## Why this basis rather than a name scan

Settings that are deliberately *not* local paths stay excluded for free, because `_read_option` never resolved them as paths in the first place:

- `ivert_results_subdir` — in `_RELATIVE_PATH_KEYS`, resolved against each DEM at validation time. It must **not** be created here, and it's excluded automatically rather than by remembering to leave it out.
- `s3_*` keys and URLs — their own skip branches.
- `icesat2_vertical_datum="ellipsoid"` — quoted, so `ast.literal_eval` returns first.
- `export_error_formats = tif,gpkg` — no path separator.

## Incidental fix

The path verdict is recomputed whenever an option is re-read, so a user config overriding a path setting with a non-path value is dropped from `path_options`. Previously, `cache_directory = none` in a user config made `setup` run `os.makedirs("none")` and create a stray relative directory in whatever directory you happened to run from:

```
$ cd /some/where && ivert setup      # before
  [created] none
```

## What you're still trusting

The `*_directory` naming convention, to tell a directory setting from a file setting. All four current directory settings follow it. A future `foo_dir` would get its parent created instead of itself — visible, not silent.

## Testing

Old-vs-new directory sets compared programmatically across the three scenarios above; `setup` output compared directly; re-read override and `ivert_results_subdir` exclusion checked. `prek` passes. `pytest` is not installed in the dev conda env.

title: Propagate config changes to settings that inherit their value
body:
## The bug

`ivert options <key>=<value>` writes only that key to `user_config.ini`. Several defaults in `ivert_defaults.ini` are defined in terms of another setting using configparser's `%(other)s` syntax, and those references resolve **inside whichever file defines them**. So overriding `user_data_directory` left every setting derived from it still resolving against the default `~/.ivert`:

```
$ ivert options user_data_directory=/mnt/external/ivert
$ ivert options list
  user_data_directory         /mnt/external/ivert     [user]
  cache_directory             ~/.ivert/cache          [default]   # wrong
  ivert_database_directory    ~/.ivert/database/...    [default]   # wrong
  ...
```

## The fix

`ivert options` now finds the affected settings — following references transitively, so `ivert_database_index` is caught via `ivert_database_directory`, and `icesat2_download_directory` via `cache_directory` — and offers to copy them into the user config:

```
$ ivert options user_data_directory=/mnt/external/ivert
  user_data_directory = /mnt/external/ivert

Warning: these settings use the value of 'user_data_directory' in their own values, and are still at IVERT's default:
    cache_directory = %(user_data_directory)s/cache
    ivert_database_directory = %(user_data_directory)s/database/granules
    ivert_database_index = %(ivert_database_directory)s/_ivert_database_index.nc
    icesat2_download_directory = %(cache_directory)s
    icesat2_requests_csv = %(user_data_directory)s/database/requests.csv
  Update them to use the new value of 'user_data_directory'? [Y/n]:
```

- Values are copied **verbatim**, `%(...)s` intact, so they resolve against the new value *and* automatically follow `user_data_directory` if it is changed again — no second prompt.
- Settings the user has already set are never listed and never overwritten. An existing `cache_directory=/fast_ssd/cache` stays, and `icesat2_download_directory` then correctly resolves to `/fast_ssd/cache` — fixing a mismatch that was already possible before.
- Only the changed settings something actually inherits from are named, so unrelated assignments in the same command are not mentioned.
- `-y`/`--yes` accepts without prompting. With no terminal to ask at (script, CI), the assignment is still saved, the inheriting settings are left alone, and a note points at `--yes`. The prompt can never abort the primary change.

## Prerequisite: decoupling `user_configfile`

`user_configfile` was `%(user_data_directory)s/user_config.ini`, which made it a dependent — but it is the one setting that cannot participate.

IVERT resolves the user config's location from `ivert_defaults.ini` *before* it can open that file, so a config file naming its own location made reads and writes disagree. A `user_configfile` value in a user config caused `ivert options` to write to a file that was never read (settings appeared saved but never loaded), and `options reset` to report no config file while one existed.

So `user_configfile` now:

- defaults to `~/.ivert/user_config.ini`, independent of `user_data_directory`. **This is a no-op for every existing install** — because reads always resolved from the defaults file, every user's config already lives at exactly that path.
- is read-only in `ivert options`, with an error explaining why and pointing at `--config` / `IVERT_USER_CONFIG`, which are resolved early enough to work.
- is ignored when found inside a user config, and commented out with a dated note (reusing the existing `comment_out_options` machinery, which grew a `reason` parameter), so the warning appears once rather than on every run.

Reads, writes and `options reset` all go through a new `Config.user_config_path`, the single answer to "which file do I read and write?". `options list`/`info` now report the file actually in use, labelled `[--config]` when overridden. `ivert setup` creates that file's real directory too.

Moving `user_data_directory` still moves the cache, granules and database; the config file stays in your home directory, like `~/.gitconfig`.

## New in `configfile.py`

`option_references()`, `Config.raw_default()`, `Config.dependent_options()`, and `Config.interpolation_support_options()`. The last is defensive: it covers a future default like `%(a)s/%(b)s` where only `a` is in the copy set, which would otherwise write an unresolvable user config. No current default hits it.

## Testing

Exercised in throwaway `HOME`s: non-interactive skip, `--yes` copy, interactive `y` and `n` over a pty, re-change propagation without a prompt, user-set values preserved, multi-assignment wording, settings with no dependents producing no prompt, migration of a pre-existing hand-edited `user_configfile`, and `--config`/`IVERT_USER_CONFIG` driving reads, writes and `reset`. Regression-checked `options` bare/`list`/`info`/`reset -y`/unknown-key errors. `prek` passes.

`pytest` is not installed in the dev conda env, so the suite was not run.

## Docs

`docs/options.md` gains "Settings that are defined in terms of other settings" and "`user_configfile` is read-only", plus a note in the priority-order list.

title: Replace the homegrown progress bar with tqdm
body:
Closes #27.

Drops `src/ivert/utils/progress_bar.py` in favour of [`tqdm`](https://github.com/tqdm/tqdm), so we no longer maintain our own bar.

### Why

The hand-rolled bar rendered poorly outside Linux terminals:

- it measured the terminal width once, in a **default argument** (`width=get_terminal_width(...)`), which Python evaluates at import time — so the width was frozen for the life of the process and ignored any resize;
- it hard-coded `█` (U+2588) as the fill character, which raises `UnicodeEncodeError` on a Windows console that isn't on a UTF-8 code page.

tqdm picks an ASCII fill automatically when the output encoding can't represent the block characters, re-measures the terminal on every redraw, and throws in a rate and an ETA for free.

### What changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/ivert/validate_dem.py` | One bar over the `N` cells, created before the polling loop and closed in a `finally` so it comes down on the exception path too. |
| `src/ivert/utils/parallel_funcs.py` | Bar created *lazily*, so the per-file and per-process reporting modes still print one line each and never show a bar. |
| `src/ivert/plot_validation_results.py` | Simplest case — wraps the iterable directly. |
| `src/ivert/utils/progress_bar.py` | Deleted. |
| `pyproject.toml` | `tqdm` added to `dependencies`. |

`tqdm` was already installed in every IVERT environment as a transitive dependency of `fetchez`, so this doesn't pull anything new into an existing install — but we now depend on it directly rather than relying on someone else's dependency tree.

### Behaviour

Preserved. `disable=None` draws the bar only when attached to a terminal, matching the old `sys.stdout.isatty()` guard, and the bars stay on **stdout** rather than moving to tqdm's default of stderr. Status lines that can interleave with a live bar now go through `tqdm.write()`, so they no longer overwrite it.

Two counting bugs are fixed along the way:

- `process_parallel` filled the bar to the index of the last process *started* while labelling it with the number *finished*; it now tracks the finished count throughout. Its "already exists" branch also advanced that count without touching the bar, which could leave the bar short of its total when a run ended on skipped files.
- In `validate_dem`, a chunk orphaned by a crashed child is now reflected in the bar immediately, rather than at the next completion.

### Testing

Exercised all four `process_parallel` reporting paths (bar-only, per-outfile, per-process-name, and the no-identifying-info fallback) plus `get_data_from_h5_or_list`, both under a pty and with output redirected — confirming the bars render and reach 100% on a terminal and stay completely silent when they aren't on one. `prek run` passes on all changed files.

Not covered: `validate_dem`'s bar wasn't exercised end-to-end, since that needs real ICESat-2 photon data. That call site was verified by review plus a standalone replica of its exact tqdm usage (create with `total`, `update()` by delta, `write()` mid-bar, `close()` in `finally`).

title: Never reuse a cached vertical shift grid that does not cover the region
body:
Closes #67.

A cached vertical shift grid could be reused for a region larger than the one it was generated over, and every point outside it silently received a **0.0 m** datum shift. An unconverted height is indistinguishable from a legitimate zero separation, so the failure was invisible: validating a Newport, OR DEM against a grid cached by an earlier, narrower run left 861 of 2,881 photons in ellipsoid heights and produced 141 grid cells offset by a constant **+24.4 m**.

## Cause

`_apply_vertical_transform()` named the cache file from bounds rounded to 0.1°:

```python
grid_fn = f"vshift_{src}_{dst}_{w:.1f}_{e:.1f}_{s:.1f}_{n:.1f}.tif"
if not os.path.exists(grid_fn):
    transformez.generate_grid(region=region_bounds, out_fn=grid_fn)
```

but generated the grid over the *exact* region. Two runs whose extents differ by less than 0.1° therefore share one file while needing different areas — here `[-124.06171, …]` and `[-124.06723, …]` both mapped to `-124.1_-124.0_44.6_44.6`. Reuse was decided by `os.path.exists` alone, and `RegularGridInterpolator` was configured with `fill_value=0.0`.

This is not a transformez bug: `generate_grid(region=…, out_fn=…)` built a grid over exactly the region it was handed, both times. The caching and the out-of-bounds fill are IVERT's.

## Changes

1. **Grids are generated over the region snapped outward to 0.1°** and named from the snapped bounds, so the file name describes exactly the extent covered and any later request landing inside that box is genuinely covered by it. `_snap_region_outward()` guards against a bound sitting on a multiple collapsing the box to zero width.
2. **A cached grid is verified before use.** `_grid_covers_region()` opens it and checks it spans the region being transformed, regenerating if it falls short or cannot be read (truncated by an interrupted run, etc.). Coverage is tested against the real data region rather than the snapped one, so a grid trimmed by a pixel of increment rounding still counts as a hit.
3. **Out-of-bounds points raise instead of returning 0.0.** `fill_value` is now NaN, and any point outside the grid raises a `ValueError` naming the file, the grid's extent, and the points' extent. In-bounds NaNs — a genuine gap in the datum model — warn and stay NaN rather than being passed through.

Also strips the `EPSG:`/compound datum prefixes *before* building the file name rather than after, so a `"EPSG:4326+4979"`-style input can no longer put a `:` into a path (illegal on Windows).

## Verification

Reproduced the original failure exactly by restoring the stale grid, then re-running the same DEM:

| | RMSE |
|---|---|
| `main`, stale grid present | 16.573 m |
| this branch, same stale grid present | **0.397 m** |

Also checked:

- An undersized grid planted under the *new* file name is detected and regenerated (14 KB → 87 KB; bounds become the full snapped box).
- `_snap_region_outward` yields a valid, containing, non-degenerate box for a normal region, for bounds sitting exactly on 0.1° multiples, and for a zero-area input.
- `_grid_covers_region` returns True for a covering grid and False for an undersized, missing, or corrupt one.
- The backstop raises: passing an explicit `src_region` smaller than the supplied points produces `ValueError: … 1 of 3 points fall outside the shift grid …`.
- `prek run --all-files` passes.

## Upgrade note

Grids cached by earlier versions carry the old naming and are ignored rather than migrated, so no stale grid can survive this change. They are dead files afterwards — deleting `vshift_*.tif` from the cache directory reclaims the space.

title: Add --classes and --min-photons to 'ivert validate', and fix bugs found alongside them
body:
Two feature additions to `ivert validate`, the behavior changes they required, and five bug fixes — three of which surfaced while investigating a bad validation run against a Newport, OR DEM.

## Features

- **`-c`/`--classes`** selects which ICESat-2 photon classes a validation runs against (default `1/6/40`), matching the option of the same name on `ivert database download`. Slash- or comma-separated; `ivert classes` lists the codes.
- **`-mp`/`--min-photons`** sets the minimum photons a grid cell must contain to be validated (default `3`, previously hard-coded).

## Behavior changes

These change the contents of validation output, so they are worth a look before merging:

- **More cells are reported at the default settings.** Results no longer carry a hard-coded `numphotons_intd >= 3` filter, which dropped sparse cells regardless of the requested minimum. Cell inclusion is now governed solely by `-mp`.
- **Interdecile trimming now applies only at 5+ photons.** Cells with 1-4 photons use every photon they contain. Previously every cell was trimmed to its 10th-90th percentile band, which discarded most or all photons in sparse cells.
- **Cells below the threshold are omitted entirely**, rather than emitted with NaN statistics and discarded downstream.
- **Removed the `median` and `diff_median` columns** from per-cell results, and `is2_med`/`error_med` from the GeoPackage/Shapefile exports. Reporting is based on the mean.
- Photon classes are now filtered once, before the per-cell arrays are copied into shared memory, rather than inside every child process.

## Bug fixes

**Found while building the features:**

- `ivert validate` silently restricted its elevation statistics to classes 1 and 40. Requested classes other than ground and bathy floor (land ice, and the `-b`/`--buildings` flag's class 7) were counted in `numphotons` but dropped before the mean/median were computed — so `--classes` would have been half-ignored without this.
- Photon-level output computed `dem_minus_is2_m` against a Series carrying a different index from the joined frame, yielding misaligned differences.

**Found while investigating a bad Newport, OR validation run:**

- **The progress bar never reached 100%.** It advanced by rows returned per chunk, but cells below `-mp` are now omitted from those rows, so it stalled at the number of validated cells rather than the number examined — 361/1389 (26%) on the Newport DEM. Progress is now measured in cells handed out to the child processes, tracked per pipe (each has at most one chunk outstanding, so the count is exact). A chunk lost to a crashed child is credited too, since it is never retried and would otherwise keep the bar from ever reaching N.
- **`-ph`/`--include-photons` crashed with `FileNotFoundError`.** The photon path was built with `str.replace("_results", "_photons")`, which rewrites *every* occurrence — including the `ivert_results` directory name — sending the file to a sibling `ivert_photons/` directory that nothing creates. It now writes alongside the rest of a DEM's output. The same mis-derived path also made the resume check never find existing photon output, re-running the whole pipeline on every `-ph` invocation.
- **Collection output names were mangled by the same idiom.** `_summary_stats.txt`, `_plot.png`, `_individual_results.csv`, and the per-DEM `_results_EMPTY.txt` all used a blanket `str.replace`, so `-n "oregon results 2024"` produced `oregon_summary_stats_2024_summary_stats.txt`. All four now swap only the trailing `_results` via `removesuffix`, matching `_error_export_filenames()`. Output is byte-identical for names that do not contain "results".

## Verification

Exercised against a Newport, OR DEM (`WGS 84 + NAVD88`, 24 granules, 2,881 photons over 1,389 overlapping cells):

- Single-DEM and collection paths both run clean; RMSE 0.526 m, 343 cells after outlier removal.
- `-ph` writes `<dem>_photons.h5` into `ivert_results/`; the file reads back with 2,881 records, and a second `-ph` run correctly reports `Work already done here.`
- Progress bar captured under a pty: `26.0% 361/1389` before, `100.0% 1389/1389` after.
- Collection run with `-n "oregon results 2024"` produces correctly-named outputs; old and new naming verified byte-identical for the default base and ordinary region names.
- `prek run --all-files` passes.

## Not included

The Newport run's original symptom — 141 cells offset by a constant ~24 m — turned out to be unrelated to this branch: a stale cached vertical-shift grid reused for a wider extent, with out-of-bounds points silently receiving a 0.0 m datum shift. It reproduces on `main`. Filed separately as #67.

title: Stale cached vertical-shift grid silently applies a 0.0 m datum shift outside its extent
body:
## Summary

`transform_points._apply_vertical_transform()` caches generated vertical shift grids under a filename whose region bounds are rounded to 0.1°, reuses any file matching that name without checking the extent it actually covers, and then interpolates with `fill_value=0.0`. When a later run covers a wider area than the cached grid, every point outside the cached extent silently receives a **0.0 m vertical shift** — the datum conversion is skipped with no error and no warning — and those points keep their source (ellipsoid) heights.

The result is validation output that looks clean but is wrong by the full geoid separation for part of the DEM.

## Observed

Validating a Newport, OR DEM (`WGS 84 + NAVD88 height`) produced a sharply bimodal error distribution:

| group | cells | `diff_mean` mean | `diff_mean` std |
|---|---|---|---|
| correct | 220 | −0.29 m | 1.43 |
| offset  | 141 | **+24.43 m** | 0.44 |

Reported RMSE was **15.315 m**. The offset cells' *within-cell* photon scatter was normal (median stddev 0.146 m, same as the good cells), so this was not noise, canopy, or sparse-cell outliers — it was a clean constant shift, matching the NAVD88↔ellipsoid separation at this location (~24 m).

All 2,881 photons were class 1 (Ground); no class 6 or 40 photons were involved.

## Root cause

Per-photon, `dem_z - z` (the shift `transform_points` applied) was:

- 2,020 photons: ~+24.0 m (correct)
- **861 photons: exactly 0.000 m**

The 861 zero-shift photons all lay at x ∈ [−124.06723, −124.06419]. The cached grid `vshift_4979_5703_-124.1_-124.0_44.6_44.6.tif`, written by an earlier run over a narrower photon set, has a left edge of **−124.06171**. Every zero-shift photon was west of it.

Three compounding defects in `src/ivert/transform_points.py`:

1. **The cache key cannot identify the grid's extent.** `grid_fn` formats the bounds as `{w:.1f}_{e:.1f}_{s:.1f}_{n:.1f}`, so regions differing by up to 0.1° collide. Here `[-124.06171, ...]` and `[-124.06723, ...]` both produced `-124.1_-124.0_44.6_44.6`.
2. **Reuse is decided by `os.path.exists(grid_fn)` alone.** The cached raster's real bounds are never compared against `region_bounds`.
3. **`RegularGridInterpolator(..., bounds_error=False, fill_value=0.0)`** makes "outside the grid" indistinguishable from a legitimate zero shift. A skipped datum conversion should not be representable as valid output.

## Confirmation

Deleting the stale grid and re-running the identical command regenerated it over the full extent (left edge −124.06723). Zero-shift photons dropped from 861 to **0**, cells with |error| > 10 m from 141 to **0**, and:

```
RMSE: 15.315 m  ->  0.526 m
```

This is not a regression from any recent branch: the same DEM on `main` (f8dc7c1) with the stale grid in place reports **RMSE 16.573 m**.

Note this is **not** a transformez bug. `transformez.generate_grid(region=..., out_fn=...)` correctly built a grid over exactly the region it was handed, both times; the caching and the out-of-bounds fill are IVERT's.

## Suggested fix

- Validate a cached grid before use: open it and confirm its bounds contain `region_bounds` (with a small tolerance), regenerating if not.
- Make the cache key lossless with respect to extent, or drop the bounds from the name and rely on the bounds check.
- Stop silently zero-filling. Use `fill_value=numpy.nan` and raise (or at minimum warn loudly and drop those points) if any point falls outside the grid, so a missing conversion can never be mistaken for a zero shift.

Users with an existing `~/.ivert/cache/` should clear `vshift_*.tif` after the fix, since already-cached grids may be undersized.

title: Handle unrecognized options in the user config file gracefully
body:
Closes #65.

## The crash

Reading a `user_config.ini` that contains an option name absent from `ivert_defaults.ini` crashed:

```
configparser.NoOptionError: No option 'old_removed_setting' in section: 'DEFAULT'
```

This happens after upgrading IVERT to a version where a setting has been renamed or removed, and also when a setting is misspelled by hand.

`_read_option()` fell through to `self._config.getboolean("DEFAULT", key)` for any value `ast.literal_eval` could not parse. That lookup goes against the *defaults* parser, so an option the defaults don't define raised. It was also returning the wrong value for options that do exist: a `yes`/`no` boolean set in the `[AWS]` section or in the user config took its value from the `[DEFAULT]` section of `ivert_defaults.ini` rather than from the override. The value is now converted directly via `ConfigParser.BOOLEAN_STATES`, which removes the crash path and fixes the override.

## Handling unrecognized options

On top of the crash fix, unrecognized options are now detected up front. `Config` compares the user config's options against every option in `ivert_defaults.ini` (`[DEFAULT]` and `[AWS]`), warns on stderr, comments them out of the user's file, and ignores them:

```
WARNING: The IVERT user config file /home/user/.ivert/user_config.ini contained settings that IVERT v0.6.6 does not recognize:
    - old_removed_setting
  They may have been renamed or removed in a newer version of IVERT, or misspelled when entered by hand.
  They have been commented out of that file (with a dated note) and ignored.
  Run 'ivert options list' to see the settings IVERT supports.
```

The file afterwards:

```ini
[DEFAULT]
# My own note about the verbosity setting.
verbosity = warning
# Automatically commented out by IVERT on 2026-08-10: unrecognized setting name.
#old_removed_setting = some/old/path
```

The rewrite is text-based rather than a `ConfigParser.write()`, so the file's own comments, blank lines, section headers, and ordering all survive. Indented multi-line values are commented out along with the assignment that starts them. If the file can't be written (read-only), the warning says so and IVERT continues on defaults. Subsequent runs are silent, since the offending lines are now comments.

Two neighboring failure modes also degrade to a warning instead of a traceback: a malformed user config file, and an interpolation reference that can't be resolved.

## Verification

Checked by hand against the reproducer from the issue and these cases:

- The exact `NoOptionError` from #65 is gone; the setting is commented out and ignored.
- Unrecognized options in both `[DEFAULT]` and `[AWS]` are caught, and re-running is silent.
- Multi-line values, `key: value` colon delimiters, and read-only config files are all handled.
- Recognized user overrides still apply, and `ivert options list` still reports them as `[user]`.
- `prek run --all-files` passes.

title: Gracefully handle changes to variables names in ivert_defaults.ini on ivert package updates.
body: When a user uses the "ivert options" command to change default options, it writes out a user_config file, in which values can override those in the ivert_defaults.ini file. Useful for customization (setting directories, file formats, etc). However, when the IVERT software is upgraded by the user to a newer versions, if the old user_config file contains variables that no longer are contained in the ivert_defaults.ini file, the configfile.py parser crashes with a configparser.NoOptionError. We need to gracefully handle IVERT reading configuration files that may have missnamed (or outdated) variables in them, without crashing.

title: Enable nine more previously-ignored ruff lint rules
body:
Second pass at trimming the `[tool.ruff.lint] ignore` list in `pyproject.toml`, following #62. This removes nine more rules and fixes the ten errors they raise. The ignore list goes from 130 to 121 entries.

As before, rules were chosen by running `ruff check src --extend-select ALL --statistics` to get the real violation count behind each ignored rule, then picking those whose fixes are mechanical and carry no behavior change.

### Rules enabled

| Rule | Sites | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `C404` unnecessary-list-comprehension-dict | 1 | `dict([(k, v), ...])` rewritten as a dict comprehension |
| `PERF401` manual-list-comprehension | 1 | append loop replaced with a list comprehension |
| `RET503` implicit-return | 1 | `_fmt_size()` restructured so its final return is reachable |
| `RUF012` mutable-class-default | 1 | mutable class attribute annotated as `ClassVar[dict[str, str]]` |
| `RUF013` implicit-optional | 1 | `classes: list = None` spelled as `classes: list \| None = None` |
| `RUF059` unused-unpacked-variable | 1 | unused unpacked `base` renamed to `_base` |
| `SIM118` in-dict-keys | 1 | config section iterated directly rather than via `.keys()` |
| `SIM212` if-expr-with-twisted-arms | 1 | `None if not datadir else datadir` → `datadir or None` |
| `UP031` printf-string-formatting | 2 | percent-format strings replaced with f-strings |

### Notes

**`RET503`** — `_fmt_size()` iterates `("B", "KB", "MB", "GB", "TB")` and returns when `nbytes < 1024 or unit == "TB"`, so the loop can never fall through and ruff's literal fix would have appended an unreachable `return None`. Instead the loop now covers `("B", "KB", "MB", "GB")` with the `TB` case returned explicitly afterward. The two forms were compared across 11 magnitudes from `0` to petabyte-scale and produce identical output for every input.

**`RUF059`** — the line `base, ext = os.path.splitext(results_dataframe_file)` appears three times in `validate_dem.py` (lines 967, 1327, 1731). The first two use `base` on the following line; only line 1731 leaves it unused, and only that one is renamed.

**`SIM212`** — ruff's suggested fix is `datadir if datadir else None`, which would immediately violate `FURB110` (enabled in #62). The `or` form satisfies both rules.

**`RUF012`** — adds `from typing import ClassVar` to `icesat2_database_v2.py`. The annotation is purely declarative; the attribute remains an ordinary class-level dict at runtime.

**`B905`** (zip-without-explicit-strict, 15 sites) is again deliberately left out. It is the one remaining low-count rule that is not mechanical: each call site needs a decision about whether the zipped iterables are guaranteed equal-length, and `strict=True` converts today's silent truncation into a `ValueError`. It deserves its own pass.

### Verification

- `ruff check src`, `ruff format --check src`, and `prek run --all-files` all pass.
- `ivert --help` and `ivert options` run; all touched modules import cleanly.
- Behavior spot-checks beyond the linter: `_fmt_size` old vs. new compared across 11 input magnitudes (no mismatches); `list(section) == list(section.keys())` confirmed against the real config for the `SIM118` change; `SIM212` equivalence checked for `""`, `None`, a path, and `"."`; the `ClassVar` dict confirmed still readable with correct values; both rewritten `ValueError` messages confirmed to render as before.
- Two modules could only be checked with `py_compile`, for environment reasons unrelated to this branch: `validate_dem.py` needs `transformez`, which is not installed locally, and `plot_results_slope_centrality.py` imports a nonexistent `import_parent_dir` module (pre-existing on `main`).

`pytest` is not installed in the local environment, so the test suite was not run.

### Remaining work

Still one step toward #40, not the whole thing. The largest remaining block is the `PTH*` cluster (~380 hits across 20 rules), a genuine `os.path` → `pathlib` refactor rather than a sweep. Other sizable groups still ignored include `ANN*`, `ERA001`, `E501`, `T201`, and `EM101`/`EM102`.

Part of #40.

title: Expand 'ivert database export' to accept .nc granule and index files
body:
Closes #59.

Expands the positional argument of `ivert database export` beyond bounding boxes and raster/vector extents. It now accepts:

- **A single IVERT `.nc` photon granule** — exported in its entirety, as a point layer. This pulls one specific granule out of the database, and (looping over the granule files) supports exporting the whole database one granule at a time. `--classes` and the date options still apply.
- **The IVERT database index `.nc` file** — exported as a *polygon* layer: one rectangle per granule, drawn from its `data_bbox`, carrying every index field. Since it holds polygons rather than points it cannot be written as `xyz`, and the photon filters do not apply to it (a note is printed if they are given).

Both are auto-detected from the file's variables (`filename`/`granule_id`/`data_bbox_*` for the index, `x`/`y`/`z`/`class_code` for a granule), and both are read straight off disk with no database lookup, so neither requires a populated local database. A `.nc` file of neither kind gives a clear error.

### Also in this PR

- **Polygon-vector region files now clip to the polygons themselves**, not just to their combined rectangular extent, so a file of disjoint polygons exports only the data inside each one. The bounding box is still used to pre-select which granules to read, and the clip is a single vectorized `shapely.intersects` call against a prepared geometry. Files with no polygonal geometry fall back to their extent, as before. This is a behavior change for polygon inputs.
- **Index shapefile output uses explicit short field aliases** (`numphotons_bathy_floor` → `n_bathyflr`, `data_bbox_xmin` → `d_xmin`, …), so all 32 index fields survive the format's 10-character field-name cap instead of colliding under GDAL's truncation.
- `IS2Database._read_index()` split into a `read_index_file(path)` classmethod, so any index file can be read and not only the configured one.

The existing bounding-box and raster-extent behavior is unchanged.

### Testing

Verified against synthetic fixtures (a photon granule, a two-record index, and a two-polygon GeoPackage):

- whole-database, bounding-box, and raster-extent exports
- polygon clip: 292 of 500 photons exported, all inside the polygons, with the 158 photons in the gap between the two polygons correctly excluded
- polygon file combined with `--classes` and a date range
- granule export with and without `-o` (default output name derives from the input file)
- index export to `gpkg` and `shp`: polygon geometry, EPSG:4326, every field present with names within the shapefile limit
- error paths: missing file, non-IVERT `.nc`, non-NetCDF file named `.nc`, and `-of xyz` against the index

`prek run --all-files` passes. `pytest` is not installed in the dev env used here, so the test suite was not run.

Docs (`docs/database.md`) and `CHANGELOG.md` updated.

title: Replace dual GPKG/Blosc database index with a single NetCDF index
body:
Closes #45.

## Summary

The database index was maintained in two formats — a GeoPackage plus a blosc-compressed pickle cache kept in sync. This replaces both with a single xarray/NetCDF (`.nc`) index file and removes the `blosc2` dependency entirely.

Config changes:
- `icesat2_granules_gpkg` + `icesat2_granules_blosc` → **`ivert_database_index`** (default `_ivert_database_index.nc`)
- `icesat2_granules_directory` → **`ivert_database_directory`**

## Design

The index is stored as a plain table of numeric columns. Granule bounding boxes are exploded into scalar `query_bbox_*` / `data_bbox_*` columns, and no geometry is serialized (the footprint is always `box(data_bbox)`). It therefore reads straight back into a `pandas.DataFrame` with no shapely reconstruction, and spatial lookups are vectorized bounding-box comparisons via a new `cuboids_intersect_vectorized()` helper.

## Performance

Read time for a 10,000-granule index (page-cache-warm):

| Format | Read | File |
|---|---:|---:|
| BLOSC (old cache) | 39 ms | 1.5 MB |
| **NetCDF (new)** | **85 ms** | 4.7 MB |
| GPKG (old primary) | 326 ms | 5.5 MB |

The NetCDF index reads ~3.8× faster than the GeoPackage it replaces. It is slower than the old blosc cache in isolation, but that cache had to be regenerated whenever the GeoPackage changed; a single self-consistent file removes that maintenance and the extra dependency.

## Changes

- **`icesat2_database_v2.py`** — single NetCDF index; `_write_index`/`_read_index` produce plain DataFrames; shared `_index_record_from_attrs` converter; vectorized rewrites of `query_granules`, the download replace-logic, `read_database_file`, `bounds()`, and `unique_bboxes()`.
- **`cuboid_funcs.py`** — new `cuboids_intersect_vectorized()` (same strict-overlap semantics as the scalar version, verified identical).
- **`validate_dem.py`** / **`pickle_blosc.py`** / **`pyproject.toml`** — remove the `blosc2` dependency and the deleted module.
- **`cli.py`**, **docs**, **default config** — updated for the new keys and single index file.

## Verification

- Round-trip of the index (columns, dtypes, values, empty DB) verified.
- `cuboids_intersect_vectorized` produces identical results to the previous per-row `cuboids_intersect` across randomized queries, and `query_granules` selects the identical granule set end-to-end.
- `ruff check` + `ruff format` clean.

title: Expand "ivert database export" to export individual files as well as bounding boxes.
body:
Right now the "ivert database export" command is set to take a bounding-box argument to define which subset of the database to export to a vector point file, or a raster data source (such as a DEM) to define the bounding box to export. This could export data from one or more ICESat-2 granules currently saved in the database.

I would like to expand the "export" functionality to also accept the following as an argument:

- A single .nc "ivert photon granule" file stored in the database, and export it in its entirety. This would be if someone wants to get the data from a particular granule (rather than all granules from within a bounding box), and also tacitly supports exporting the entire database one file at a time by simply looping over all the granule files.
- The vector database-index file (currently stored as a .gpkg in IVERT v0.6.6), which is a polygon vector file rather than a point file. IVERT would recognize when the database index is being exported to another format, and adapt accordingly to exporting it as a polygon vector file.

The existing bounding-box functionality would remain unchanged; it would simply add options to the "ivert database export" command.

title: Add 'ivert database export' command to export photons to vector formats
body:
Builds on #55 (`ivert classes`). Targets the `add-ivert-classes-command` branch so it can be reviewed as a stacked PR; it will retarget to `main` automatically once #55 merges.

## Summary

Adds a new `ivert database export` subcommand that exports IVERT ICESat-2 photons to common GIS vector formats.

- **Formats** (`-of/--output-format`): `gpkg` (default), `shp`, `xyz`, or a comma-separated combination (e.g. `gpkg,shp`).
- **Region**: export the entire database, or restrict to one geographic area given as a bounding box (`--wsen` / `-p` supported, matching `download`) or a georeferenced raster/polygon-vector file.
- **Filtering**: `-c/--classes` (slash-separated codes) and a date range (`-ds/--start-date`, `-de/--end-date`, dateparser formats).
- **Safety**: large exports prompt for confirmation unless `-f/--force` is given.
- Outputs carry the full per-photon field set (`x, y, z, class_code, class_name, confidence, delta_time, granule_id, bathy_confidence`); shapefiles drop the two fields that exceed the format's limits.

## Implementation notes

- `export_vector.py` is refactored into a pure library backing the command (format/subset/multi-write helpers added) and its standalone CLI is removed, since it is no longer needed.
- New command lives in the `database` group in `cli.py`, mirroring `database download`'s region-parsing style.

## Docs

- New `## export` section in `docs/database.md` plus examples.
- New `docs/classes.md` documenting `ivert classes`, linked from the README.

## Testing

Verified end-to-end against a local 20-granule database: full export, multi-format (gpkg+shp+xyz), bbox subset, class filter, date-range narrowing, vector-file region, overwrite-skip, and error cases. `ruff check`/`ruff format` pass via pre-commit.

title: Add 'ivert classes' command and centralize photon class definitions
body:
## Summary

Adds a top-level `ivert classes` command that lists the ICESat-2 photon classification codes and their meanings, and eliminates the duplicated class definitions that had drifted out of sync across the codebase.

## Changes

- **New `ivert classes` command** — prints each photon class code and its description.
- **New `src/ivert/photon_classes.py`** — single source of truth. Parses the definitions from globato's `ATL03Reader.meta_desc` so IVERT stays in sync with the upstream classifier. Exposes `photon_classes()`, `class_descriptions()`, `class_labels()`, and `class_names()`.
- **Removed drift-prone duplicates:**
  - `export_vector.py` — deleted the hard-coded `CLASS_NAMES` dict; now uses `class_names()`.
  - `cli.py` download `--classes` help — replaced the hand-maintained code list with a pointer to `ivert classes`.
  - `plot_photon_clouds_v2.py` — dropped the class list in the header comment and the `label=` entries baked into `CLASS_STYLE`; legend labels now come from `class_labels()` (colors/z-order unchanged).
- **`database download` default classes** updated `1/6/7/9/40/41/42` → `1/6/7/40/41/42/44`: drop `9` (not a class globato assigns) and add `44` (Open Ocean Surface).

## Companion label changes (globato)

Because definitions are now sourced from globato, the water/seafloor class **labels** are being clarified upstream in [continuous-dems/globato#133](https://github.com/continuous-dems/globato/pull/133):

| Code | globato label |
|---|---|
| 40 | Seafloor |
| 41 | Nearshore Water Surface |
| 42 | Inland Water Surface |
| 44 | Open Ocean Surface |

Once that merges and the installed globato updates, `ivert classes`, exported `class_name` strings, and plot legends reflect these automatically — no further IVERT change required.

## Behavioral notes

- New downloads now include class `44` (Open Ocean Surface) photons and no longer request the inert `9`. Existing local databases are unaffected.
- Exported `class_name` attribute strings now derive from globato rather than the old hard-coded names. With globato#133, the resulting names are `canopy_top`→`top_canopy`, `building`→`buildings`, `bathy_floor`→`seafloor`, `bathy_surface`→`nearshore_water_surface` (`inland_water_surface` is unchanged). Anything downstream that parses those strings should be aware.

## Testing

- `ruff check src` and `ruff format --check` pass (all pre-commit hooks pass).

title: Default 'ivert validate -ex' bboxes to W/E/S/N order with --wsen flag
body:
## Summary

The \`-ex\`/\`--exclude\` bounding boxes in \`ivert validate\` were parsed in W/S/E/N (\`minx/miny/maxx/maxy\`) order, inconsistent with \`ivert database\` commands, which default to W/E/S/N (\`minx/maxx/miny/maxy\`) with an opt-in \`--wsen\` flag.

This PR makes \`ivert validate\` behave the same way:

- \`-ex\`/\`--exclude\` bounding boxes now default to **W/E/S/N** (\`minx/maxx/miny/maxy\`).
- A new \`--wsen\` flag switches interpretation to **W/S/E/N** (\`minx/miny/maxx/maxy\`), mirroring \`ivert database download\`.
- Downstream \`validate_dem\` still receives \`(minx, miny, maxx, maxy)\` tuples, so nothing below the CLI layer changes.

## Changes

- \`_parse_exclude_spec(value, wsen=False)\` reorders the four values based on the flag and returns the same tuple shape as before.
- Updated \`-ex\`/\`--exclude\` help text to document the new default order and the \`--wsen\` switch.
- Added the \`--wsen\` flag to the \`validate\` command and threaded it through.

## Verification

- \`_parse_exclude_spec('1/2/3/4')\` → \`(1.0, 3.0, 2.0, 4.0)\` (default W/E/S/N)
- \`_parse_exclude_spec('1/2/3/4', wsen=True)\` → \`(1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0)\` (W/S/E/N)
- \`ivert validate --help\` shows the updated \`-ex\` help and the new \`--wsen\` option.

title: Add coverage summary stats and --minimum-coverage-pct filter to validate
body:
## Summary

Adds coverage-aware reporting and filtering to `ivert validate`, plus a couple of small `_summary_stats.txt` improvements.

### Coverage summary statistics
When `-mc/--measure-coverage` is used, `_summary_stats.txt` now includes a decile section reporting the RMSE of grid cells above each coverage threshold (from 100% of cells down to the best-covered 10%). This shows how ICESat-2 coverage — and thus sampling bias — affects reported DEM accuracy.

### `--minimum-coverage-pct` / `-mcp` filter
New option on `ivert validate` that drops grid cells whose measured coverage is below a given percentage (0-100) from **all** outputs: the `_results.h5` dataframe, `_summary_stats.txt`, error exports, and plots.

- Requires `-mc/--measure-coverage`; using it without that flag raises a clear usage error.
- Value is constrained to the 0-100 range.
- Threaded through the single-DEM, multi-DEM (collection), and DEM-subdivision code paths. Because coverage is a per-cell property, per-subset filtering yields identical merged results.

### `_summary_stats.txt` polish
- Reduced excessive float precision to 2 decimal places (at least 2 significant digits for magnitudes below 0.10).
- Reordered so the "Number of cells with bathymetry photons" and "Mean roughness" lines appear above the "== Decile ranges of errors" section.

## Testing
- All three edited modules compile; ruff check/format pass.
- CLI verified: option appears in `--help`, the `-mc`-required guard fires, and out-of-range values are rejected.
- Filtering verified end-to-end against a synthetic results dataframe (a ≥50% threshold retained exactly the expected cells).
- No existing unit tests cover this path (the `src/tests/` files are integration download scripts).

- **`ivert options list --details`** (`-d`): lists every setting with its description; the plain `list` footer now advertises both new views.
- **Bug fix in `_OptionsGroup`**: subcommands taking positional arguments (like `info <name>`) were being misrouted to the `key=value` setter. The bare-assignment case is now flagged explicitly during `parse_args`, which also avoids Click's deprecated `protected_args`.

title: Cross-platform compatibility fixes for Windows and macOS
body:
## Summary

Fixes a set of cross-platform compatibility issues so IVERT runs on modern Windows and macOS as well as Linux. Each fix preserves existing Linux behavior. No functional change on Linux.

## Fixes

- **Config path resolution (`configfile.py`)** — Path detection was gated on `sys.platform`: the Windows branch only recognized values containing a backslash, but the `.ini` files use forward slashes (e.g. `~/.ivert`). On Windows those values fell through unhandled, leaving `~` unexpanded. Replaced the two platform-specific branches with one platform-agnostic branch (treats a value as a path if it contains `~`, `/`, or `\`) plus an `_is_absolute_path()` helper that recognizes Unix, Windows drive, and UNC roots regardless of OS. On Windows `~/.ivert` now resolves to `C:\Users\<user>\.ivert`.

- **`signal.SIGKILL` guard (`validate_dem.py`)** — `signal.SIGKILL` does not exist on Windows, so `abs(exitcode) == abs(signal.SIGKILL)` raised `AttributeError` whenever a validation subprocess exited non-zero. Look the attribute up with `getattr` and skip the OOM-killer recovery branch when it is absent (Windows has no SIGKILL / OOM-killer); a failed worker now surfaces as the intended `RuntimeError`.

- **Cross-platform terminal colors (`bcolors.py`)** — Raw ANSI escape codes render on Linux/macOS but appear as literal garbage on Windows consoles, where virtual-terminal processing is off by default. Enable it on import via `colorama.just_fix_windows_console()` (no-op elsewhere; only sets the console-mode flag, does not wrap `sys.stdout`, so it does not interfere with `loggerproc.Logger`'s stdout redirection). `colorama` added as a Windows-only dependency; the import is defensive so Linux/macOS degrade to native ANSI.

- **Multiprocessing start method (`validate_dem.py`, `validate_dem_collection.py`)** — `set_start_method("spawn")` raises `RuntimeError` if the start method was already set. Pass `force=True` so re-invocation cannot crash.

- **Explicit UTF-8 encoding** — Text-mode `open()` defaults to the platform locale encoding (e.g. cp1252 on Windows). Pass `encoding="utf-8"` on all text-mode opens (empty-result markers, summary stats, user config, photon-tile lists, the AWS datasource probe, and the process logger). Binary opens are unchanged.

## Testing

Verified on Linux: config paths still resolve to the correct absolute home-directory locations; the SIGKILL decision logic was unit-checked across POSIX/Windows exit-code cases; bcolors imports and renders (VT-enable is a no-op on Linux and degrades gracefully if colorama is absent); `set_start_method(force=True)` is idempotent; and no text-mode `open()` without an encoding remains. `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass on all changed files.

Not covered here (requires real Windows/macOS hardware): the shared-memory + `spawn` parallel-validation path in `validate_dem.py` — Windows frees named `SharedMemory` segments when the last handle closes, unlike Linux `/dev/shm`, so that flow should be exercised directly on the target platform.

- Exercised `generate_result_geotiff`, all four error-export formats (`tif`/`gpkg`/`shp`/`xyz`), and `split_dem` with the pre-port GDAL code, then re-ran identically after the port: all 63 comparisons match exactly (pixel values, transforms, CRS, nodata, dtypes, point geometries, and attribute values).

title: Fix icesat2_vertical_datum config being silently ignored by globato
body:
## Summary
- `_process_h5_to_nc()` passed an EPSG code string (`"EPSG:4979"`/`"EPSG:3855"`) as globato.read()'s `vertical_datum` kwarg.
- globato's `ICESat2Reader` only recognizes the literal strings `"ellipsoid"`, `"ellipsoid-mean-tide"`, `"geoid"`, `"geoid-mean-tide"`, and silently falls back to `"ellipsoid"` for anything else instead of raising.
- Net effect: IVERT's `icesat2_vertical_datum` config setting had no effect on the heights globato actually produced — you always got ellipsoid heights back, regardless of what was configured, while the database/granule metadata could still claim `EPSG:3855` (geoid) if that's what was requested.

Found while tracking down a separate bug (continuous-dems/globato#127) where bathy_floor photon heights came out geoid-referenced regardless of requested datum — that turned out to be a different bug inside globato itself, but investigating it surfaced this one in IVERT's own call site.

## Fix
- Added `_EPSG_TO_GLOBATO_VERTICAL_DATUM`, an explicit lookup from IVERT's EPSG-code representation to globato's accepted literal strings.
- Added `_vertical_epsg_to_globato_datum()`, which does the lookup and raises `ValueError` if the EPSG code has no known mapping, or if the mapped literal isn't one globato's reader currently accepts (checked against `_GLOBATO_ACCEPTED_VERTICAL_DATUMS`, kept separate so a future change to globato's vocabulary is caught explicitly instead of silently mis-mapping again).
- `_process_h5_to_nc()` now calls this at the `globato.read()` call site instead of passing the EPSG string straight through. The EPSG-code representation is unchanged everywhere else (config validation, database/granule metadata storage).

title: Remove gdal and osgeo dependencies.
body:
The github.com/continuous-dems enviromnent has taken steps to remove "gdal" and "osgeo" python library dependencies in order to improve cross-platform compatibility and ease-of-install (the gdal-binaries installation, on platforms like Windows, is at times a technical barrier for users). Viable replacements for these libraries include "rasterio", "shapely", and "geopandas". Tasks:

- Replace all gdal and osgeo library calls with equivalent "rasterio", "shapely", and "geopandas" implementations.
- Test each component code-base to ensure identical functionality.
- Remove all "import gdal" and "import osgeo" statements from the ivert code-base.

title: ivert validate: add --omit flag to exclude photons within bounding box or polygon geometry
body:
## Summary

Add an `--omit` flag to the `ivert validate` subcommand that allows users to exclude ICESat-2 photons falling within specified geographic regions from being used in DEM validation.

## Motivation

Some validation areas may contain known artifacts, construction zones, water bodies, or other regions where photon data should not be used. A spatial exclusion filter lets users cleanly omit those areas without preprocessing the input DEMs or photon data.

## Proposed Interface

```
ivert validate --omit <geometry> [other options] <DEM files>
```

The `--omit` flag should accept:

- **Bounding box** — four space-separated or comma-separated floats in W/E/S/N order (e.g. `--omit -70.5 -70.0 43.2 43.8`)
- **Vector file** — path to a polygon vector file (`.shp`, `.gpkg`, or `.geojson`); all features in the file are treated as exclusion zones

The flag may be specified multiple times to combine multiple exclusion regions.

## Implementation Notes

- Exclusion should be applied after photon retrieval but before photon-to-DEM comparison, so that excluded photons do not contribute to statistics or plots.
- For bounding-box input, convert to a simple rectangular polygon for a uniform internal representation.
- For vector files, use the file's native CRS (reproject to WGS84 if needed) and perform a point-in-polygon test against the photon lat/lon coordinates.
- `geopandas` / `shapely` are natural fits for the spatial filtering step; confirm they are available or add them as dependencies.
- The exclusion geometry (or a summary of it) should be noted in output metadata and logs so results are reproducible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--omit <W> <E> <S> <N>` correctly excludes photons inside the bounding box
- [ ] `--omit <file.shp/.gpkg/.geojson>` correctly excludes photons inside any polygon in the file
- [ ] Multiple `--omit` arguments can be combined
- [ ] Excluded regions are reported in validation output/logs
- [ ] Existing validation behavior is unchanged when `--omit` is not specified
- [ ] Tests cover bounding-box and vector-file exclusion paths

title: Lint and format all source files with ruff
body:
## Summary

Adopt [ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) as the project's linter and formatter, replacing (or supplementing) the current `pylint` + `flake8` setup.

## Motivation

- `ruff` is significantly faster than `pylint`/`flake8` and covers most of the same rules
- Provides an integrated auto-formatter (`ruff format`) that can replace `black` or ad-hoc style fixes
- Single tool for linting + formatting reduces CI complexity
- Can be configured via `pyproject.toml` alongside existing project metadata

## Proposed Work

1. Add `ruff` as a dev dependency in `pyproject.toml`
2. Add a `[tool.ruff]` (and `[tool.ruff.lint]`) configuration section to `pyproject.toml`:
   - Select an appropriate rule set (e.g., `E`, `F`, `W`, `I`, `UP`, `B`)
   - Add any project-specific ignores to avoid noise during the initial pass
3. Run `ruff format src/` and commit formatting changes
4. Run `ruff check --fix src/` to apply auto-fixable lint issues; manually resolve the rest
5. Update CI (`.github/workflows/`) to run `ruff check src/` and `ruff format --check src/` in place of (or alongside) `pylint`/`flake8`
6. Decide whether to keep `pylint`/`flake8` for rules `ruff` does not cover, or remove them

## Acceptance Criteria

- `ruff check src/` exits with code 0
- `ruff format --check src/` exits with code 0
- CI enforces both checks on every PR
- `pyproject.toml` documents the chosen rule set and any intentional ignores

title: Replace argparse with click for CLI argument parsing
body:
## Summary

The CLI currently uses Python's `argparse` module for argument parsing. Migrate all argument parsing to [Click](https://click.palletsprojects.com/) to improve composability, testability, and user experience.

## Motivation

- Click provides a cleaner decorator-based API that keeps argument definitions co-located with the command function
- Built-in support for subcommands maps naturally to IVERT's existing subcommand structure (`validate`, `download`, `import`, `status`, `upload`, `test`, `subscribe`, `upgrade`)
- Better help text formatting and automatic `--help` generation
- Easier to test commands in isolation via `click.testing.CliRunner`
- Supports parameter types, callbacks, and environment variable overrides with less boilerplate

## Proposed Work

1. Add `click` as a dependency in `pyproject.toml`
2. Audit all files in `src/` that use `argparse` (`ArgumentParser`, `add_argument`, `parse_args`, etc.)
3. Refactor each parser into Click commands/groups:
   - Top-level `ivert` CLI → `@click.group()`
   - Each subcommand → `@cli.command()` with `@click.option()` / `@click.argument()` decorators
4. Replace `argparse.Namespace` usage throughout with Click's parameter passing
5. Update or add `CliRunner`-based tests for each subcommand
6. Verify `ivert --help` and per-subcommand `--help` output is correct after migration

## Acceptance Criteria

- No `argparse` imports remain in `src/`
- All existing CLI subcommands work identically from a user perspective
- `ivert --help` and `ivert <subcommand> --help` produce well-formatted output
- At least smoke-test coverage via `click.testing.CliRunner`

title: Replace print() statements with logging throughout codebase
body:
## Summary

The codebase currently uses `print()` statements for output and diagnostics throughout the source. These should be replaced with proper Python `logging` entries so that log levels, formatting, and output destinations can be controlled at runtime.

## Motivation

- `print()` cannot be suppressed, filtered, or redirected without wrapping the process
- `logging` supports configurable levels (`DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`), making it easy to increase or decrease verbosity
- Structured logging integrates better with server environments, cloud deployments, and monitoring tools
- Consistent use of `logging` makes it easier to trace issues in production

## Proposed Work

1. Audit all `src/` files for `print()` calls
2. Introduce (or extend) a logging configuration in the package — likely in `src/ivert/__init__.py` or a dedicated `src/ivert/logging_config.py`
3. Replace each `print()` with an appropriate `logging.<level>()` call:
   - Diagnostic/verbose output → `logging.debug()`
   - Normal progress messages → `logging.info()`
   - Recoverable issues → `logging.warning()`
   - Errors → `logging.error()` or `logging.exception()`
4. Ensure the CLI (`src/client.py`) configures the root logger based on a `--verbose` / `--quiet` flag (or existing equivalent)
5. Update tests if any assert on stdout output

## Acceptance Criteria

- No `print()` calls remain in `src/` (except intentional user-facing output where `logging` is inappropriate, e.g., formatted table output via `tabulate` — document any exceptions)
- Log level is configurable at runtime
- Existing behavior is preserved; no regressions in tests or CLI usage

title: Convert IVERT client install to setuptools
body:
Currently, the IVERT client is installed on a user's machine with the src/ivert_new_user_setup.py script. There are a few issues with this:

- The current setup script makes several assumptions about dependencies, etc, that are not checked.
- It's a multistep process and could be simplified. Users (who may or may-not be familiar with git) have to clone the repository, then run the "src/ivert.py setup" script.
- After install, it currently requires users to run "src/ivert.py", but it is not in a user's "path" directory.

Python Setuptools can help with that, requiring a user to do just one (maybe two) to install and being using IVERT from anywhere in their environment.
